memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments and his sons and their garments." - Lev 8:30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Oil and blood, sprinkled together.

Throughout Scripture, blood speaks of atonement and oil speaks of the Spirit's anointing. Here they are mingled and applied at once.

That combination is not accidental. There is no anointing of the Spirit apart from the atoning work that makes a person fit to receive Him. And atonement was never meant to leave a person merely forgiven and unequipped.

Peter announced both together at Pentecost: Repent and be baptised, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:38). Forgiveness and the Spirit, given together.

Paul says God anointed us, set his seal of ownership on us, and put his Spirit in our hearts as a deposit (2 Cor 1:21-22).

Some Christians live as though they have received the blood but not the oil — forgiven, but powerless and passive. Others chase the oil while neglecting the blood, wanting spiritual experience without dealing honestly with sin.

God sprinkled both on Aaron in the same motion. He does not divide what He has joined.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I living as forgiven but not empowered?
2. Do I seek spiritual experience while avoiding honest dealing with sin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for both the blood that cleanses me and the Spirit who fills me. Let me live in the fullness of both. Amen.
